subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming acceptance criteria (FastFin pilot)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fastfin.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming acceptance criteria (FastFin pilot)

Hi Laura / Adam —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed acceptance criteria we discussed for the pilot so engineering and product can align: 

Summary of goals
- Interactive assistants on the dashboard (fast, low-latency text responses)
- Support short conversational turns (avg. 40–120 tokens) and code-like snippets occasionally

Performance targets (proposal)
- TTFT (first token): P50 < 80ms, P95 < 180ms for typical 40–120 token responses
- Sustained throughput for pilot: 120 QPS (concurrent interactive users ~40, concurrency per user ~3)
- Burst tolerance: 300 QPS for 30s without headroom failures

Streaming and UX constraints
- Streaming preferred for token-by-token UI (WebSocket recommended when P95 chunk cadence target <300ms)
- SSE acceptable for looser cadence (>300ms) or if you want simplified client implementation
- Chunk cadence: target 100–250ms between meaningful token chunks (we suggest chunking at ~32–64 token boundaries for your average payloads)

Risk/notes
- If you need strict P95 TTFT <100ms globally we should discuss Dedicated capacity + colocated region routing
- We’ll provide a pilot runbook with measurements and a simple SDK example for both WS and SSE clients

Next steps
1) Marcus to validate sizing and share a pilot scope + initial cost estimate (attachment) — ETA: Aug 23
2) FastFin to confirm whether they will use WebSocket or SSE for the dashboard UI — please confirm by Aug 24
3) Schedule a short engineering sync (30m) to align on auth and telemetry schema — propose Aug 26 or Aug 27

Attaching a one-page pilot scope and rough TTFT band sizing. Let us know if any numbers should be moved tighter or looser.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fastfin_pilot_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet), ttft_band_sizing.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming acceptance criteria (FastFin pilot)

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our engineering/product leads: 

1) TTFT P95 of 180ms — is that measured from TCP accept (public API) or from within a private VPC path? We need to ensure comparisons to our in-app metrics are apples-to-apples.
2) For chunk cadence, you mentioned 32–64 token chunking. Does Redwood provide a client-side reassembler or do we need to handle partial token merges when using SSE?
3) If we opt for WebSocket, do you support automatic reconnects with KV-cache warm restoration or will we need to reinitialize per reconnect?

We lean toward WebSocket for the dashboard because we want snappy token-level UI, but we'll confirm with frontend by EOD Aug 24. Also curious about what observability you’ll provide during the pilot (latency breakdown by token, per-route traces).

—Laura
Laura Chen
VP Product, FastFin

Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming acceptance criteria (FastFin pilot)

Laura —

Good questions, quick technical answers below. Adding concrete options so you can pick the trade-offs.

1) TTFT measurement point
- Default: measured at the Redwood public API ingress (time from request arrival to first byte emitted). For Private/VPC deployments we can surface in-VPC metrics that exclude public network variance. We’ll include both in the pilot reports.

2) Client-side handling for SSE vs WS
- WebSocket: we stream token deltas over a persistent socket. We support idempotent resume tokens so KV cache warm restoration is possible on reconnect (recommended for low-latency reconnections).
- SSE: simpler reassembly (newline-delimited chunks). No automatic resume — reconnect triggers a new session and model context must be rehydrated (we can provide a lightweight checkpointing pattern).

3) Chunking cadence & chunk size guidance
- Recommendation for FastFin dashboard: 48-token chunk target, cadence goal 120–200ms for P50; P95 will be ~2–2.5x higher depending on region and concurrency.
- If you push cadence below ~90–100ms consistently, we recommend per-route Dedicated instances to keep tail latency consistent.

4) Observability during pilot
- We’ll provide per-request traces, TTFT histograms (P50/P90/P95/P99), per-route cost breakdown and a streaming chunk cadence histogram. We’ll publish a short dashboard link for the pilot (read-only).

Attachments: ttft_band_sizing.pdf (estimates), streaming_cadence_notes.txt (sample client pseudocode for WS + SSE).

I attached a small sizing doc that maps your 120QPS sustained target to a recommended instance footprint and expected cost range. If you want, we can run a 2-hour synthetic stress run against a mirror endpoint to validate P95s at your expected concurrency — we typically do this during pilot kickoff.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Laura / Adam —

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn. Following up with concrete mutual action items and a suggested schedule: 

Mutual action plan (MAP)
- By Aug 24 (EOD): FastFin confirms WS vs SSE (you indicated preference for WS) — ACTION: Laura
- By Aug 25: Redwood provides final pilot scope spreadsheet + DocuSign for the pilot agreement — ACTION: Marcus/Olga (attachment enclosed)
- Aug 26 (11:00am PT): Engineering sync (30m) — agenda: auth flow, telemetry schema, demo client choice (WS vs SSE) — ACTION: all
- Aug 28: 2-hour smoke/stress run against mirror endpoint to validate TTFT P95 and chunk cadence — outcome: test report and recommended tweaks

Acceptance criteria (to mark pilot success)
- TTFT: P50 < 80ms, P95 < 180ms (measured at chosen ingress; we’ll publish both public and in-VPC numbers)
- Chunk cadence: median 120–200ms and 95th percentile < 400ms for first 30s of interactive sessions
- Error rate: <0.5% 5xx across pilot duration

Please confirm the MAP and we’ll lock calendar invites. If you want an updated cost delta for Dedicated routing to tighten P95 to <100ms, we can include that as an optional line item in the pilot agreement.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a short technical kickoff.

Warmly,
Olga
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
